findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed several cans on the shelves to be dented. The dented cans were removed from the shelves by the inspector and set aside by the PIC. The inspector suggests increasing the frequency that employees check the condition of product. Employees should also be educated on the importance of removing dented cans from service. Ensure that food packages are always in good condition to protect food from potential contaminants.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed multiple foods (including, but not limited to, cookies and crackers) stored in baskets directly on the floor. The PIC was educated that food must be stored at least 6-inches above the floor. Ensure that the food is moved 6-inches above the ground by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed there is a buildup of ice on the condenser and product underneath the condenser in the back walk-in freezer. The buildup may be due to the large volume of product inside the freezer. Ensure that the buildup of ice is removed to create a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a wall of solid ice along the back of the walk-in freezer coming from the overhead condenser and covering numerous carboard boxes full of food. At the time of inspection, food is inaccessible due to an excessive amount of food stored in the freezer. Operator states that until recently they have been unable to cancel freezer shipments to the facility. The freezer is not adequately sized for the foods held inside. Due to the complete covering of food product with ice that must eventually be thawed, these items are considered contaminated and must be removed from stock. Additionally, foods that must be removed to access the condenser unit and ice must remain frozen during any work being performed in the freezer to prevent temperature abuse of these items. Operator states that a work-order is being placed to repair the freezer and prevent future accumulations. However, foods which are contaminated and those which are not must be separated in the meantime and contaminated foods must be removed from the freezer. Once cleared, DO NOT place foods directly under the condenser unit until it has been repaired/cleared. Inspector will return on Friday 12/8/2023  to evaluate clearing of the cooler and removal of potentially contaminated foods as well as cleaning of the floor and pallets where spills have occurred.

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
The walk-in freezer is not sufficient in capacity to hold the amount of frozen foods the facility possesses. Either the amount of food must be reduced or additional freezer space must be provided. Currently, due to the lack of space, cleaning and maintenance of the walk-in freezer is not easily accomplished. Due to the time of year and historically long waits for maintenance, an additional 60 day follow-up is issued to ensure that the freezer has been repaired. Inspector will return on or around 02/05/2024 to ensure that corrective actions have been taken.

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.
